summary.headline: Transpek Q1 FY27 revenue fell 6.5% YoY to INR155.1 crore and EBITDA fell 32.4% to INR24.1 crore, with a 15.6% margin.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR155.1 crore, down 6.5% YoY, with EBITDA of INR24.1 crore (down 32.4% YoY) and a 15.6% margin, and PAT of INR8.9 crore. Management attributed the decline to aggressive pricing, oversupply and subdued export demand. The company remains net debt-free. Management said it is moving to a more aggressive growth stance, with an Odisha greenfield site (INR250 crore over 5-6 years, subject to board approval) and a multi-purpose pilot plant at Ekalbara. The DuPont contract, now assigned to Arclin, continues on unchanged terms, with renewal talks expected between Q4 CY26 and Q1 CY27.

segments.name: Polymers (end-user application)
segments.commentary: Largest end-user segment at 48.7% of Q1 revenue; down from 60-65% a few years ago to roughly 45-50% over time as the portfolio diversified.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: 18.7% of Q1 revenue; management cited rising contribution from organic peroxides, dyes and surfactants during the quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at least 15% over FY26 (about 15-20% stated), with acid chloride sales to rise from about INR4 crore to about INR15 crore this year.
Target to double business size in 5 years; management said the strategy is finalised.
EBITDA margin guided at 15-20% going forward, with product-wise margins varying.

New products: one product expected to add about INR50 crore annual revenue, with commercialisation near year-end FY27 and revenue from next year; a second product expected to add about INR50 crore annually; several others could add INR50-100 crore each.
Odisha greenfield project: board decision targeted within 25-30 days; construction could start by end-November 2026 if approved; commercial production 1.5-2 years after start; payback 4-5 years.
Multi-purpose pilot plant at Ekalbara: 6-7 months to build, around February 2027.
Management said the company expects to run all four sites at full permitted capacity this quarter.
capex_capacity: Odisha greenfield capex of about INR250 crore over 5-6 years in multiple phases, pending board approval and feasibility study; DuPont-linked capex in the past was about INR110 crore.
Multi-purpose pilot plant (four streams, multi-step chemistry, fluorination, distillation) being built at Ekalbara; about 6-7 months to complete.
Effective capacity utilisation of about 70-75% (best case 80-82%) because capacity is product-specific and permits are 20-30% below the sum of stream capacities.
Expansion blocked at Ekalbara (about 10 years of approvals pending) and Dahej (about 1.5 years for permissions). Of three job-work sites, two are in the same Ekalbara area.
Management said about INR200 crore of capex over the last 5-6 years was largely replacement and captive thionyl chloride capacity, not growth capex.
demand_pricing: Pricing pressure from Indian and global competitors; price erosion in some products. Open-market acid chloride pricing is competitive, while Arclin pricing is formula-based cost-plus.

Arclin (ex-DuPont) contract assigned in full with the same terms. Management said Arclin's order volumes are rising this quarter, and the contract is a pass-through for raw materials; rupee depreciation is passed on to the customer.
Management said it is in talks with about 2 customers on sizeable contracts, but decisions are being delayed.
Electronics-grade trimethylbenzoyl chloride (TMBC/246 TMBC, for photoinitiators) is being developed for one large customer; purification work is ongoing.
Management said there were no product discontinuations, though some product demand fell sharply in certain quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Growth has lagged the 10-12% CAGR previously guided (FY19 revenue INR595 crore vs FY26 INR621 crore, EBITDA INR117 crore vs INR80 crore); would the company consider a buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said estimates are not guaranteed due to cycles, guided at least 15% revenue growth for FY27, and said the board sees buybacks as lower-return than reinvesting in growth.

qa_highlights.question: What happens if the Arclin/DuPont contract is not renewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no reason for non-renewal (nine-year supplier, no rejected kilos, no missed deliveries) but is preparing for a worst case; a non-renewal would be a significant blow to volume and margins, with recovery taking time.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the INR300 crore Silox investment not being monetised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the stake is illiquid under the shareholder agreement; the partner has been offered the stake but has not bought it, and no near-term resolution is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US tariff advantage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no special tariff; Transpek pays the normal 18% rate, and customers receive duty drawbacks.

qa_highlights.question: Why expand capacity when utilisation is only 70-75%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said permissions at Ekalbara are blocked, product-specific streams require a mix, and Odisha is needed for new products.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex now being committed ahead of demand, and what revenue do the new products add?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is investing partly ahead of demand. It said two products could add about INR50 crore each annually, and that the INR150-200 crore guided earlier had not yet materialised.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected IRR or payback on the INR250 crore Odisha project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said payback would be 4-5 years.

risks_watch: Arclin/DuPont renewal (talks expected Q4 CY26 to Q1 CY27); the contract is a large share of volume and margins.
Margin pressure from competition and from volatile raw material prices (management cited a jump from about $2,600/t to $4,000/t within 10 days).
Odisha board approval and permit timing; the 2 to 1.5 year execution timeline is long.
New product commercialisation has slipped in the past (a battery electrolyte product was stopped after a technology change).
Silox stake (about INR300 crore) remains illiquid with no near-term monetisation.
Management said the West Asia conflict and logistics are a risk to global demand.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term strategy and the balance sheet, but cautious on near-term demand and pricing. Management was evasive on Silox monetisation, contract volumes and product-level margin disclosure, and gave specific but unverified timelines for new products and Odisha.
key_quotes: Transpek has been a consistent 9-year supplier now. Without not a single kilo even rejected by the customer in terms of quality.
Margins, of course, we have to target, and we are targeting 15% to 20% overall margins.
We are looking at almost INR 250 Crores over 5-6 years.

adds.what: Odisha greenfield site, multi-phase (pending board approval and feasibility study)
Multi-purpose pilot plant at Ekalbara (four streams, multi-step chemistry, fluorination, distillation)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of at least 15% and a target to double business in 5 years, with an INR250 crore Odisha greenfield plan over 5-6 years, but Q1 revenue fell 6.5% YoY, utilisation is only about 70-75% effective (80% best case), and the Odisha project is not yet board-approved, so the outlook is positive but not clearly backed by new capacity coming live near term.
